message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. LeBron quickly became known for his combination of size, athleticism, and basketball IQ, earning the nickname “King James.” Over his career, he has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers, winning multiple NBA championships and earning numerous MVP awards.

Beyond the court, LeBron is also a philanthropist, entrepreneur, and media personality. He founded the LeBron James Family Foundation, which focuses on education initiatives such as the I PROMISE School in Akron. He has also produced films and television shows through his production company, SpringHill Entertainment, and has been involved in various business ventures, including a partnership with Nike and ownership stakes in several sports teams.
